title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
summary: BeNice! replaces independent per-recurrence KV-caches in looped transformers with a single shared cache, broadcasting the final recurrence's KV into the first recurrence and post-training it to produce compatible residuals. The cost is a two-stage pipeline (stochastic-depth pretraining plus a BeNice! post-training stage) and added training complexity; inference quality reportedly matches standard finetuning perplexity. It can fail because KV-shareability is not a reliable property of looped models even with identical training, so the post-training stage may not restore quality for a given checkpoint.
rationale: The method requires pretraining with stochastic depth and applies only to looped architectures, which the reader neither trains nor typically deploys, though it is worth monitoring for adoption by looped-model providers.
technique: KV-sharing across recurrences in looped models

claims.statement: BeNice! replaces independent per-recurrence KV-caches in looped transformers with a single shared cache, broadcasting the final recurrence's KV into the first recurrence and post-training it to produce compatible residuals. The cost is a two-stage pipeline (stochastic-depth pretraining plus a BeNice! post-training stage) and added training complexity; inference quality reportedly matches standard finetuning perplexity. It can fail because KV-shareability is not a reliable property of looped models even with identical training, so the post-training stage may not restore quality for a given checkpoint.
In simulated low-memory long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.
